Definition: perhaps from the base of G5494 in the sense of its congener the base of G5490 (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument):--hand.
BiblicalUsage: The hand is the instrument of power and of touch, and it is everywhere in the New Testament. The eye cannot say to the hand that it has no need of it, Peter tells us to humble ourselves under the mighty hand of God, Thomas is told to behold the hands of the risen Christ, and Jesus shows His hands and feet to the disciples.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the hand of God is both mighty and pierced: it humbles us and it saves us, and the risen hands still bear the marks. My hand has its place in the body, and His hand has me.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Appears to Thomas; Jesus Appears to the Disciples on Easter Evening
